original_question: Let b(P) be the minimum size of a blocking set Q for a finite point set P in general position, and let b(n) be the minimum of b(P) over all n-point sets with no three points collinear. Prove that b(n)/n tends to infinity as n tends to infinity.
target_in_paper: Section 2.4, Open Problem 7 (Blockers of Visibility Graphs): prove that the minimum blocker number b(n) for n-point sets in general position is superlinear, i.e. that b(n)/n→∞.
correct_elements: The draft identifies the correct open problem, the correct asymptotic claim, and the right quantities b(P) and b(n): it is about blockers for planar n-point sets in general position and asks to prove that b(n)/n tends to infinity.
missing_details: The ambient space should be stated explicitly: all point sets lie in the Euclidean plane R^2.
The blocking set Q should be required to be disjoint from P.
The blocking condition should be defined explicitly: every open segment determined by two points of P must contain at least one point of Q.
It should be stated that b(P) is the minimum cardinality of such a set Q.
It should be stated explicitly that b(n) is minimized over all n-point sets P in the plane with no three points collinear.

The paper frames the claim as a superlinear lower bound on b(n); the refined question should preserve that exact asymptotic scope and not drift to midpoint sets, blocked-coloring variants, or obstacle-number variants.
refined_question: Let P be a finite set of points in the Euclidean plane in general position (that is, no three points of P are collinear). Define b(P) to be the minimum cardinality of a set Q ⊂ R^2 \ P such that every open segment with endpoints in P contains at least one point of Q. For each n, define b(n) := min{ b(P) : P ⊂ R^2, |P| = n, and no three points of P are collinear }. Prove that lim_{n→∞} b(n)/n = ∞.
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, prove that b(n)=ω(n), i.e. the minimum possible number of blockers for an n-point set in general position is superlinear in n.
justification: This draft is targeting the paper's blockers subsection, specifically Section 2.4, Open Problem 7, not a neighboring problem. Immediately before that statement, the paper introduces blocking sets and the functions b(P) and b(n) in the precise no-three-collinear regime relevant here. It then says that many authors conjecture a super-linear number of blockers and states Open Problem 7: prove that b(n)/n tends to infinity. Your draft is therefore already very close to the paper's official formulation; the main missing items are the planar setting, the requirement Q∩P=∅, and the explicit definition that Q must meet every open segment determined by two points of P. Also, although the prompt mentions Conjecture 1.1/Proposition 1.2/Theorem 1.3, those labels are not the relevant target in arXiv:1012.5187; the relevant labeled statement here is Section 2.4, Open Problem 7.
